purpose: Raw evidence store for the benchmark-aware router. Nothing reads this file at runtime. scripts/compile_benchmark_frontiers.py transforms it deterministically into skill/benchmark_frontiers.json, which is the compact derived layer the routing rules cite. Three layers, kept separate on purpose: RAW EVIDENCE (this file) -> DERIVED FRONTIER (generated, never hand-edited) -> RUNTIME ROUTING RULE (skill/SKILL.md prose).
rules_of_use: Two numbers are comparable only when they share a comparability_group. Groups are authored, never inferred: a group asserts that benchmark, version, harness, tool access, scaffold and evaluator were held constant across its rows.
Never interpolate a score between effort levels. A missing rung is null, not an estimate.
null means 'not published'. It is never a placeholder for a guess.

A vendor_relative row (one vendor's harness measuring a competitor) is direction evidence, not a settled ranking. It outranks nothing that a model_intrinsic or ecosystem_end_to_end row covers. A vendor_relative row that favours the COMPETITOR is against-interest and is the most credible kind of vendor evidence.
An aggregate index never overrides a task-specific benchmark for a task that benchmark covers.
Where groups disagree and no precedence rule resolves them, the compiler must emit UNRESOLVED. It must never average, split the difference, or pick the newer number.

source_tiers.A: Primary: model vendor's own docs, launch post or system card, read directly.
source_tiers.B: Benchmark owner or serious independent evaluator (Artificial Analysis, Vals, benchmark leaderboards).
source_tiers.C: Blogs, aggregators, search-index relays of a primary page that could not be fetched, and figures this repo carried forward without re-verification. Signal only; never the sole basis of a rule.

evidence_classes.model_intrinsic: Same evaluator AND same agent harness/scaffold across every model in the group. Answers 'which model is stronger, holding the stack constant'. The right input for model + effort selection.
evidence_classes.ecosystem_end_to_end: Each model runs inside its own vendor's agent stack (Claude Code + Claude vs Codex CLI + GPT). Answers 'how does the stack this user would actually run perform on this task family'. The right input for the RECOMMENDED AI badge. Never read as 'model A intrinsically beats model B'.
evidence_classes.vendor_relative: One vendor's harness applied to itself and to a competitor. Direction only.
evidence_classes.aggregate: A composite index spanning several task families. Admitted for effort-rung comparisons within one model, token-load comparisons, and a last-resort tie-break only.
evidence_classes.efficiency_only: Carries no capability score -- tokens, cost or latency only.
evidence_classes.unclassified: Provenance not established well enough to assign a class. Cannot support a rule.

evidence_precedence.note: Used by the compiler when comparability groups disagree about direction. Higher wins. Ties, or a win by less than one full step, produce UNRESOLVED.

model_ecosystem.note: Declared, never inferred from the model name. Legacy models are included because they appear in older rows; the compiler ignores any model not on a current roster.

direction_setting_hierarchy.note: The ONLY bases on which a comparability group may set a direction, in order. A group whose equivalence_band names none of these sets no direction, however large the gap looks. Replaces the old no_dispersion_rule, which fell back to 0.15 x the roster's observed score spread: that reads as statistics and is not one. Spread is how far apart the models happen to sit, not how precisely either score was measured, and on a two-row cell the spread IS the gap, so every comparison would have 'won'. The compiler now refuses min_fraction_of_spread outright so the fallback cannot come back by accident.

order.note: e.g. the Terminal-Bench owner leaderboard's 95% CI whiskers -- a value the record does not yet carry, which is why the AA TB 4.0 cells are UNRESOLVED rather than a Codex win
95% interval by the conventional multiplier; applies_to scopes it to the benchmark it was published for

order.band: 2 x SD over repeated runs under one harness
order.note: reproducible dispersion, e.g. a mean over 5 attempts with its spread stated

order.band: the threshold the benchmark owner publishes
order.note: an explicit practical-significance bar stated by whoever runs the benchmark -- not one this repo invents
UNRESOLVED for that evidence cell. The router falls through to the efficiency tie-break and says low-confidence.

direction_setting_hierarchy.observed_spread_is_diagnostic_only: The compiler still emits observed_spread and gap_over_observed_spread_diagnostic per cell. They are there to show which cells are worth chasing a published interval for. They never set a direction.
direction_setting_hierarchy.consequence: After this change only the Terminal-Bench-Science cells carry a real band (SE +/-3.5-4.5, published by Anthropic). Every other capability direction is UNRESOLVED at this layer. That does not make SKILL.md's badge table wrong -- the badge is ranked by provenance (Step 6 order: gate, capability, WHO RAN IT, parity, efficiency), not by significance -- but it does mean no direction in this record is statistically certified except science.

excluded_from_direction.reason: Epoch AI runs FrontierMath, but the source itself discloses that OpenAI funded its development and holds exclusive access to part of it. A benchmark one party paid for and can partly see cannot settle a comparison between that party and a competitor. The rows stay in the evidence store; they set no direction.

The two vendors' published accounts of the same model are irreconcilable -- OpenAI's table puts Opus 5 at 30.2 while Anthropic's Opus 5 launch note claims 'three times the nearest competitor' -- and neither publishes a harness spec that would explain the gap.
Saturated: the frontier clusters within about one point and no source states the scaffold. A benchmark that cannot separate the candidates cannot inform a routing rule.
Mutable snapshot with no dataset identifier or checksum, not reproducible from the owner's repo, and the per-category rows this repo relied on through iteration-14 could not be re-verified.
Superseded index version. AA's current Coding Agent Index puts the same model at 62 where this one says 67, so the two are not comparable and only the current version may set a direction.
Provenance never established -- the figures could not be traced to any live index. Superseded by the AA Coding Agent Index rows, which are the real thing.

routing_rules.note: Authored link from a rule in skill/SKILL.md to the evidence records behind it. The validator checks that every evidence_id resolves to a record. comparison_type says what KIND of question the evidence answers, which is what decides whether it may drive model selection, the badge, or only an efficiency tie-break.

Tooled HLE is AGAINST OpenAI's interest and favours Claude; FrontierMath favours Astra but Epoch's own disclosure says OpenAI funded it and holds partial exclusive access; ARC-AGI-3 contradicts Anthropic's own claim. Net: keep Claude, keep low-confidence, cite the against-interest row.

The owner's leaderboard columns are Rank/Model/Agent/Resolution rate/Cost/Tokens with 95% CI whiskers -- per-model token and CI data EXISTS here. Tooled gap Fable 5.1 vs Opus 5 = 1.4 points; tool-less gap = 4.3. Tools compress the frontier gap -- the Opus-4.8-era 'tools close the gap' finding survives into this generation, and it is why the tool-less clause still routes upward while tooled work does not. No Codex model on either row: the deep-reasoning cross-ecosystem call is evidence-poor.

Only 2.8 points behind Opus 5 here, against ~15 on Terminal-Bench 4.0. Same capability label, very different gap -- 'agentic coding' is not one number. IDE-agent scaffold vs terminal scaffold is the likely cause, which is why the router splits agentic-code from terminal-tool.

This repo previously refused to use GDPval at all, because a 3-Elo Sonnet-vs-Opus claim was inside the noise. A 113-Elo Fable-5.1-vs-Sol gap is a different magnitude and IS usable as direction. GDPval-AA v2 is also one third of the AA Index's Agents category (30% weight).

Partial and strict scoring differ by ~36 points on the SAME model and version. Any OSWorld comparison that does not state the scoring mode is unusable -- which is exactly the problem with the Astra 72.6 row below.

Absolute pass rates are low (17-31%) for everyone: the benchmark is unsaturated, so ratios read larger than the underlying capability difference. Use as direction, not as 'Fable 5.1 is 1.6x better at workflows'. AutomationBench-AA is also one third of the AA Index's Agents category.
Listed as 'max with fallback'.

1 index point below max at 17% less cost and a third of the latency.

DOMINATED. Opus 5 at high scores 48 for $3.61, and Opus 5 at xhigh scores 50 for $4.88 -- both stronger AND cheaper than Sonnet 5 at max (38 for $5.09). This is the evidence behind 'the router never emits Sonnet 5 . max' and behind the escalation target being Opus 5 . xhigh. Sonnet 5 at high/xhigh was not in the extract; those rungs are unknown, not inferred.

Sol at high (42, $0.81) matches Terra at max (42, $1.40) at 42% less cost -- the Codex mirror of the Sonnet-5-max dominance. Sol at xhigh is NOT published here; do not interpolate it.

Fastest output in the whole table (112 tok/s) at the lowest cost/task ($0.18) -- and, at max, it ties Sonnet 5 at max on the index for 4% of the price. Basis of the volume-gate recommendation going to Codex. The router still emits Luna . low there: the gate exists because the task needs no depth.

Claim is relative only: 'more than doubles Opus 4.8 at a lower cost per task'. No absolute score published, so no cross-model comparison is possible from it. Recorded because the 5-attempt mean IS a repeated-trial design -- the kind of dispersion the equivalence rule prefers when a CI is missing.
One of the very few published REASONING-token figures anywhere. Generation-over-generation, not cross-vendor, so it cannot settle a Claude-vs-Codex efficiency question.
